function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you pull the node‑level data for **fabric `test-de`**.  
The telemetry function we have available (`telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get`) requires a few pieces of information that identify the exact node and pod you’re interested in:

| Parameter | What it’s for | Example value |
|-----------|---------------|---------------|
| `fabricName` | Name of the fabric | `"test-de"` |
| `nodeId` | Numeric ID of the node | e.g., `101` |
| `podId` | Numeric ID of the pod | e.g., `5` |
| `interfaceType` | Type of interface you want info on | `"svi"`, `"ethernet"`, `"loopback"`, or `"port-channel"` |
| `infoType` | Kind of data you want | `"interfaces"`, `"status"`, `"statistics"`, or `"errors"` |

Because you only mentioned the fabric name and the IP address (`23.31.32.1`), we’ll need the **node ID** (and optionally the pod ID) to make a precise request. If you can provide those, I can show you the exact function call and the expected JSON response.

If you’re not sure what the node ID is, you can usually find it in your fabric inventory or by querying the fabric’s REST API (e.g., `/api/fabrics/test-de/nodes`). Once you have that, let me know and I’ll walk you through the next steps!
